mechanisms.label: Atlantic barrels replace Gulf supply
mechanisms.summary: The available evidence indicates a shift in import origins from the Persian Gulf to Atlantic sources. 1) Japan’s April crude imports fell to a record low because of Persian Gulf tanker disruptions, prompting a pivot to U.S. crude. 2) China’s recent oil scramble has redirected demand toward West African barrels, raising Angola and Congo crude premiums.  These observations support the mechanism that buyers are structurally replacing Gulf barrels with Atlantic (Americas/Africa) supply rather than making a one‑off substitution.
